name: Nepheline

matrix.title: Prism length × prism modification
matrix.subtitle: Stout six- or twelve-sided prisms with flat {0001} summits. Point group 6 is polar, so the top and bottom pedions and pyramids are separate forms; here they are kept equal, because visible hemimorphism is rare.
matrix.note: Six interfacial angles match Dana (1892) to within 0.12°, for example c∧p = 44.05° against 44°5′. Natural crystals are often poorly formed.

about: Nepheline is the main feldspathoid of silica-undersaturated alkaline rocks. Its habit is simple: short six- or twelve-sided prisms ({101̄0} ± {112̄0}) capped by a dominant basal face, sometimes bevelled by the pyramid {101̄1}. Nepheline composition has long been used as a crystallization-temperature indicator (Hamilton 1961).

habits.name: Modified summits
habits.text: Pyramid bevels on the summit edges (column 12p).

references.citation: Gatta, G.D., Angel, R.J. (2007). Elastic behavior and pressure-induced structural evolution of nepheline: implications for the nature of the modulated superstructure. American Mineralogist 92, 1446–1455.
Tait, K.T., Sokolova, E., Hawthorne, F.C., Khomyakov, A.P. (2003). The crystal chemistry of nepheline. The Canadian Mineralogist 41, 61–70.
Hamilton, D.L. (1961). Nephelines as crystallization temperature indicators. The Journal of Geology 69, 321–329.
